13:23 Local Time, 11:23 GMT, 16:53 IST: South Africa fought hard for most of the first session, but the innings disintegrated rapidly after the visitors took the second new ball. Josh Hazlewood achieved a career-best performance and was the pick of the bowlers in the 4th innings, but this Test match was all about Matt Renshaw - his scores of 190 and 82 were probably the difference between the two teams and he then chipped in with two crucial wickets in South Africa's second innings. The home team will look back at moments that cost them this match; they had the visitors at 124 for 6 on the first day and let them off the hook. Renshaw was superb, but the home bowlers lost the line and length that had worked so well until then. The left-hander's career-best knock took his team to 390, which is a very good score at this venue - no team has lost in Durban after making 350 or more in the first innings and it was true here as well.

South Africa's reply consisted of soft dismissals: seven batters passed 25, but none surpassed David Bedingham's 49. These starts needed to be converted into substantial scores, but some poor dismissals meant they finished with 284 - handing Australia a 106-run first-innings lead. The visitors then batted aggressively, scoring at more than 5 RPO for most of the 58 overs and declared with a lead of 420. Asked to bat for 4 sessions, the home team needed a good start and some solid partnerships, but neither materialized. Despite a couple of 50+ partnerships, including Aiden Markram's hard-fought 75, the hosts were bowled out for 206, handing Temba Bavuma his 1st Test defeat as South Africa's captain. Josh Hazlewood was a menace with the ball throughout the second innings, and it was only fitting that he finished off the match with his 8th wicket of the game. Stay tuned for the presentations..
